s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic hand dermatitis with atopic background
salient_findings: Positive patch testing reactions to multiple allergens
Long-standing history of atopic diseases including asthma and rhinitis
key_facts: 18 years history of chronic hand eczema
Onset of hand eczema occurred in early childhood
Medical history includes asthma and rhinitis
Positive family history for atopy
Limited contact with irritants
HECSI score was 244 of 360 at initial presentation
Positive reactions to nickel, cobalt, and other allergens on patch testing
Very severe hand eczema according to validated photographic guide

shortlist.label: Atopic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: 18 years history of chronic hand eczema with onset in early childhood and positive family history for atopy

shortlist.label: Allergic contact dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive reactions to nickel, cobalt, and other allergens on patch testing

shortlist.label: Dyshidrotic eczema
shortlist.why_kept: Very severe hand eczema according to validated photographic guide and HECSI score of 244

shortlist.label: Irritant contact dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Limited contact with irritants, but still a possible contributing factor

shortlist.label: Nummular dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic hand dermatitis with atopic background and possible coinfection

raw.rationale: The patient's history of chronic hand eczema since childhood, combined with a medical history of asthma and rhinitis, and a positive family history for atopy, strongly supports a diagnosis of atopic dermatitis. The presence of very severe hand eczema and high HECSI score also aligns with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Allergic contact dermatitis
rejected.why: While the patient has positive patch testing results, the onset of hand eczema in early childhood and the presence of atopy suggest that atopic dermatitis is a more likely primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dyshidrotic eczema
rejected.why: There is no specific mention of the characteristic vesicular lesions of dyshidrotic eczema, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Irritant contact dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's limited contact with irritants makes this diagnosis less likely, and the presence of atopy and asthma points towards atopic dermatitis.

rejected.label: Nummular dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation of very severe hand eczema and the absence of characteristic nummular lesions make this diagnosis less likely.
